newsitem.title: USA: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - back to unchanged ahead of CPI.
newsitem.headline: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - back to unchanged ahead of CPI.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds recovered from a slight dip to around unchanged in late afternoon trade on Tuesday after taking a second look at the latest retail sales data and deciding it was not so negative.

Still, traders were a bit queasy ahead of Wednesday's release of the Consumer Price Index, which bulls hope will confirm that the economy has yet to succumb to inflation. And the bond market's recent drive higher has curtailed buying by individual investors.
"There's some anxiety going into the inflation numbers and we've gone through some levels that make it a little difficult to push into retail," a trader said.

A municipal bond analyst said that intermediate debt fared the best in new offerings. "New issue pricing was firm overall and strong in the intermediate range. It started off with competively sold intermediate high-grades and moved over to the negotiated (sales)."
Despite the drop in yields, new issuers have not leaped in with refundings, though it has not escaped their notice.

"We're constantly looking for opportunities to do a refunding but that remains to be seen. It's all a matter of inches but we are generally in a low-interest rate environment so we are alert to that. So we'll see if an opportunity presents itself," said a spokesman for the Massachusetts treasurer. Massachusetts last tapped debt markets when it sold about $300 million of general obligations in June.
Traders noted the secondary market remained fairly quiet, and supplies are lean. The Standard and Poor's Corp Blue list, a gauge of the secondary market stood at almost $955 million.

The latest data on retail sales in June, which rose 0.5 percent, higher than the 0.2 percent rise that was predicted, initally weighed on fixed-income markets. But a downward revision in May sales, which were changed to down 0.3 percent from 0.1 percent, undercut the bearishness of the June data.

September municipal bond futures traded in Chicago ended up four ticks to 119-16/32, September Treasury bond futures were flat at 113-30/32. This left the MOB spread a few ticks firmer at plus 178 ticks.
In the secondary market, Dade County, Florida, Water and Sewer System Revenues of 2021, which pay a 5-1/4 percent coupon, were offered at 5.38 percent, NET, unchanged.
And Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, Airport Revenues of 2027, which pay a 5.4 percent coupon, were offered at 99-1/4, flat.
